page.layout: Running head at top centre with page number at top right; two medallion portraits side by side at the top, with their legends around the rims; one text column below them, full width; no marginal notes; no text below the main text.

main_text.p: NICEPHORVS Phocas Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 4922. à Christo nato 960. Cum Saracenis sæpe ac feliciter congressus est, qui Calabriam, Siciliam, Candiam, Cilicia & Cyprum occuparant: in Sicilia res haud ita bene per duces acta est: ipse Ciliciam, & bonam Asiæ partem lætis recepit auspiciis: mox Antiochiam noctu aggressus, pulsis Saracenis imperio eam adiecit. Invisus omnibus fuit, quòd bellorum prætextu novis tributis & exactionibus populum expilaret, numismata adulteraret, ac pondus imminueret: quare odiosus civibus, facile à Joanne Zimisce, noctu dormiens in cubili occiditur: intromittente etiam sicarios, Theophania Nicephori uxore. imperat annos decem. Vide Egnat. Ro. prin. lib. 2. & Cosmograp. Mun. de Græcia lib. 4.

JOANNES Zimisces occiso, ut dixi, Nicephoro, post eum imperat Constantinopoli, an. mun. 4932. à Christo nato 970. Hic clarus antea militari laude, in Roxolanos feliciter movet, Bulgariamque totam, quam sibi[?] Roxolani vendicabant, imperio subiicit, Sphendoslauo eorum Rege ad deditionem coacto. Basilium & Constantinum fratres, Romani secundi supradicti filios, Cæsares facit, ac imperij consortes creat: Nicephoro deditos è medio tollit: & damnatos exilio ab eodem, reducit. At mox parta de Roxolanis victoria, cum triumphantis specie Constantinopolim ingressus esset, veneno potatur, post annum imperij sextum. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Medallion portraits: left, a bearded man in a crown or helmet, legend PHOCAS on the left rim and NICEPHORVS on the right rim; right, a bearded man with a crown, legend ZIMISCEN (last letter doubtful) on the left rim and JOANNES on the right rim. The line "JOANNES" in the medallion is written as printed; the medallion legends are placed before the text. Doubtful: "sibi" is partly obscured by a stain in the printed line, read as "sibi" with [?]. Long s has been normalised to s; u/v and i/j normalised to modern usage (Inuisus as Invisus, Ioanne as Joanne). The page number is printed as "143" at top right.
